header:
Date: 2025-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Moore (Redwood SE), Karen Delgado (Aurora Head of Security), Raj Patel (Aurora Cloud Architect), Maya Lin (Aurora Procurement)
summary: Discovery focusing on Aurora's security and compliance requirements while they evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Key concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO (SAML/SCIM) integration, RBAC/least-privilege, comprehensive audit logs, customer-managed KMS/HSM options, data residency and retention for PII. Redwood to provide artifacts and follow up with a technical deep dive and bench plan.
topics: SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 status and artifacts
SSO/SAML & SCIM provisioning, IdP metadata exchange
Audit logging, retention, and SIEM/ELK exports
Encryption at rest and in-transit, CMK via KMS/HSM
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, isolation, egress/networking)
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: Okay thanks everyone for joining, we have about 55 minutes on the call. Quick intros from Redwood, I am Priya Shah, account owner, and Ethan Moore will be the SE today.
[00:09] Karen: Hi I'm Karen Delgado, Head of Security at Aurora, and with me are Raj our cloud architect and Maya from procurement.
[00:16] Ethan: great, thanks. The goal for today is to go over your security posture questions and figure out hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
[00:24] Raj: Right, high level we need to understand SOC2/ISO evidence, how SSO works with SAML, RBAC, what audit logs look like, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys. Also retention for PII — our compliance folks are picky.
[00:38] Priya: Totally — that's exactly what we'll cover. Quick note, some of our doc names get garbled in auto transcripts so I'll send the packet after the call.
[00:46] Karen: Perfect. First, can you confirm Redwood's certifications — SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001? We need certs and the scope.
[00:54] Priya: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001; I'll attach the certs and the SOC2 report summary. We redact vendor notes but provide the auditor attestation. The scope covers hosted control plane and our managed inference service. For Private deployments the customer-run environment falls under your own attestation.
[01:14] Raj: For private/on-prem, if the control plane is split, do you provide an air-gapped installer?
[01:20] Ethan: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped customers but usually that's an enterprise engagement. There's a private control plane option where telemetry is minimized and audit logs can be routed to your SIEM.
[01:31] Maya: On procurement side, we'll need liability language and a standard encryption and key ownership clause.
[01:36] Priya: Noted — we'll include standard contract language and propose an enterprise addendum.
[01:41] [02:05] Karen: About SSO — do you support SAML and SCIM? Our IdP is Okta. We need SCIM for provisioning and SAML for login. Also just-in-time provision?
[02:16] Ethan: Yes SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We support IdP metadata exchange and can share the SP metadata. There's also an API for service-to-service tokens — we'll map out RBAC roles.
[02:30] Raj: On RBAC, we need least privilege. Can you do token scoping limiting model access and project-level separation?
[02:38] Ethan: We have project-level RBAC, role types (admin, developer, read-only) and token scoping per project and model. For Dedicated we can map to VLANs and separate GPU pools. For Private you own the infra so you can restrict at network and IAM layer.
[02:56] Karen: Audit logs — what do they contain? Do you log prompts, responses, token metadata? And what's the retention policy out of the box?
[03:07] Priya: By default we capture request metadata, user id, timestamp, model and token counts. Prompts and responses are redacted by default in hosted unless you opt-in for logging for troubleshooting. Audit logs can be exported to S3, BigQuery, or a syslog endpoint and retention is configurable.
[03:27] Raj: We cannot have raw prompts stored in the hosted service — PII flows through prompts. Can you guarantee not persisting prompts and responses?
[03:34] Ethan: Customers can opt to disable persistent user content logging; we have prefix/KV cache behavior that doesn't persist full payloads unless logging is enabled. For strict compliance, many customers choose Dedicated or Private so that data never leaves their VPC.
[03:53] Karen: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? HSM? We need envelope encryption and key rotation policies in place.
[03:59] Ethan: Hosted supports CMEK via integration with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) where we use customer-managed keys for data at rest. For Dedicated we can support customer KMS and bring-your-own-HSM models. Private deployments can integrate with your on-prem HSMs.
[04:19] Raj: Network egress — will requests from hosted need to go through your NAT? We need to ensure egress IPs are stable for our firewall rules.
[04:27] Priya: For hosted we publish a list of stable egress IP ranges per region; for Dedicated and Private you control egress. We'll share our network diagram.
[04:35] Maya: Retention for audit logs — how configurable? Our retention is 7 years for some regulatory data. Can you store logs that long?
[04:44] Ethan: Yes, logs exported to your S3/GCS can be retained as you configure. Redwood's hosted retention defaults are shorter, but exports allow you to push to long-term archival. For logs kept in our system we can extend retention on enterprise plans.
[04:58] [06:02] Karen: Do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed audit records? Our audit team asks for proof of integrity.
[06:10] Ethan: We can provide checksum hashes and support pushing logs to immutable storage buckets. For high-assurance customers we recommend routing logs directly to your SIEM or an append-only store.
[06:21] Raj: On the subject of data residency — can you ensure data stays in EU region for GDPR?
[06:26] Priya: Yes region pinning is supported. Hosted customers can select region and we enforce data residency for storage and processing; Dedicated and Private are fully in your control.
[06:37] Karen: Encryption in transit? TLS?
[06:40] Ethan: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, mTLS is supported for private endpoints.
[06:46] Karen: Pen test and vuln scanning cadence?
[06:49] Priya: We run annual third-party penetration tests and monthly internal scanning; we'll share the summary and remediation timelines.
[06:58] Raj: How about model artifacts, model weights — do you ever store customer-provided models? We might want to bring our own model.
[07:05] Ethan: You can bring your own model in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we support model hosting but with clear contract around IP and retention. For BYOM in Private, all weights remain in your environment.
[07:18] [08:00] Karen: Compliance questionnaires — will you fill our security spreadsheet (SIG, or Laika?)
[08:05] Priya: We typically complete the SIG (Standard Information Gathering) and can share a pre-filled version. For very large questionnaires we'll coordinate with our security team.
[08:13] Maya: Procurement requirements — can you provide standard cyber insurance and subcontractor flow-downs?
[08:18] Priya: Yes we'll share typical attestation and insurance limits; any special flow-downs we can review in a follow-up.
[08:25] Raj: On logging again — if we run a POC on Dedicated, can we stream raw request logs to our ELK?
[08:32] Ethan: Yes, Dedicated supports streaming audit logs to your SIEM in near real-time. We also support S3 export or direct Kafka streams for high-volume customers.
[08:44] Karen: There's often confusion around inference caching — is any cached prefix or KV stored on disk that could persist user data?
[08:52] Ethan: Cache is memory-first and ephemeral, and in Dedicated/Private you control persistence policies. We'll document exact cache behavior; for high-sensitivity workflows customers typically disable persistent caches.
[09:06] [10:00] Priya: I'd like to propose next steps: I'll send the security artifacts, Ethan will schedule a technical deep dive with Raj about KMS and network flows, and we'll propose a scoped POC for a dedicated cluster if you want isolation.
[10:15] Karen: Sounds good. Timeline — procurement wants pilot started by mid-July, is that realistic?
[10:20] Maya: We have a go/no-go meeting on 2025-07-14.
[10:25] Ethan: Mid-July is tight but possible for a POC with a small dedicated pool; for Private it will take longer due to provisioning. We'll outline required network and firewall rules in the POC plan.
[10:38] Raj: One more technical detail — do you support VPC peering or private link for the hosted control plane?
[10:44] Priya: We have private link support for enterprise tiers and VPC peering patterns for Dedicated. We'll include architecture diagrams.
[10:52] Karen: Any default data deletion guarantees? If we terminate contract, how long will data persist?
[10:56] Ethan: We have a documented data retention and deletion policy — by default we purge customer data within 30 days of termination unless you request a longer hold. For Dedicated/Private you control retention. We'll send the policy.
[11:11] [12:00] Raj: Are there any known limitations to SAML flows — for example if we need signed assertions with certain attributes?
[12:08] Ethan: We support signed assertions and attribute mapping. We'll review your metadata and map attributes (email, groups) to our RBAC model.
[12:20] Maya: Pricing and liability aside, what's the blocker to us choosing Hosted with CMEK?
[12:27] Priya: Hosted with CMEK covers many concerns, but customers with strict regulatory needs sometimes want Dedicated or Private to ensure network and log isolation. If you require no prompt persistence and strict egress control, Dedicated might be cleaner.
[12:43] Karen: For auditability, we want tamper-proof evidence. Could you provide samples of the audit logs to validate fields?
[12:50] Ethan: We'll share a sanitized example and a dictionary of fields (timestamp, user_id, request_id, model, token_count, sha256 of payload).
[12:59] Priya: I'll follow up with that and the SOC2 docs. Anything else from Aurora?
[13:05] Raj: Could you include an expected network firewall rules doc — ports, IP ranges, and sample security group settings?
[13:11] Priya: Yes — adding to action items.
[13:15] Maya: Procurement will want SLA language and ramp pricing for Dedicated.
[13:19] Priya: We'll include a starter SOW and pricing template for pilot.
[13:24] [13:30] Karen: OK good recap. This call was helpful.
[13:33] Priya: Great — recap: we send security packet, schedule technical deep dive for KMS and network, provide bench plan for dedicated POC, and customer sends SAML metadata and retention requirements.
[13:45] Maya: We'll aim to have approvals for the pilot by 2025-07-14.
[13:49] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[13:53] [56:55] End of recording

Notes on transcript fidelity: automated transcription had occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache transcribed as KV cash). There may be speaker attribution inaccuracies.
